statements.status_notes: See CVE-2026-33870 entry on netty-codec-http. Mirrored here so scanners that flag netty-transport receive the same not_affected statement.
statements.impact_statement: Scanner over-match: the vulnerable code lives in netty-codec-http (see the sibling assessment above). OWASP Dependency-Check and similar CPE-based scanners propagate the CVE onto netty-transport via the broad cpe:2.3:a:netty:netty:* match. netty-transport ships no HTTP/1.1 chunked decoder, so even if it were exposed as a server (which Liquibase is not), the affected code path would not run from this artifact.

statements.status_notes: Netty's epoll transport fails to detect and close TCP connections that receive a RST after being half-closed, leading to stale channels that are never cleaned up and, in some code paths, a 100% CPU busy-loop in the event loop thread.
statements.impact_statement: Scanner over-match: the vulnerable code lives in netty-transport-native-epoll (see the sibling assessment above). The NVD description itself scopes the bug to "Netty's epoll transport" — EpollSocketChannel's handling of a TCP RST received on a half-closed connection — which only exists in the native epoll(7) transport implementation. The cpe:2.3:a:netty:netty:* CPE causes CPE-based scanners to propagate the CVE onto every netty-transport-* artifact, including the base netty-transport module, which ships only the abstract channel/event-loop interfaces and the pure-Java NIO transport (NioSocketChannel) — no epoll-specific code at all. Independently, a repo-wide grep for Netty server bootstrap usage (`grep -rln "ServerBootstrap" --include="*.java" .`) returns zero hits: Liquibase is a database migration CLI tool that never runs a network server. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver, used only as a client-side transport for outbound connections, so even the genuinely-affected epoll transport has no inbound socket for an attacker to exploit.
